deepseek-v4-pro → llama-1b high-stakes probe

2 run(s) · 1810 distinct conversations · new samples per iteration, not cumulative
Each tab holds only the samples new to that iteration — the redteam_postprocessed_iter{N}.jsonl dumps are near-cumulative, so a row is listed under the first iteration whose dump contains it. Iteration N's dump is what trained probe_iter{N}.pkl and is built from the red-team successes of iterations 0–(N−1). filter_dataset re-runs over the whole accumulated set before every retrain, so the new-success count is generally lower than the successes logged for that red-team iteration. Each card pairs a red-team success (left) with the contrastive rewrite generated from it (right); the kind and label filters pick which side is shown, while the search matches either half so you keep the comparison.
Probe quality on the held-out eval splits, per retrain cycle. iter0 is the baseline probe — trained on the base data before any red-teaming, so it has no sample tab; iterN is the probe retrained on the data in the “Iteration N” tab (cumulatively). Hover a chart for the values at that iteration.
The same three retrain cycles run again with a slice of the red-team data removed, to see which slice the probe was actually losing ground to. Every arm shares the base training data, the split seed and the eval splits, so the only variable is which pairs were dropped — identical inputs give an identical probe, so equal lines mean the pruning had nothing to remove at that iteration rather than that it made no difference.
